subject: Re: Reliability SLO follow-up / competitive evaluation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Smith <jenna.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reliability SLO follow-up / competitive evaluation

Jenna, thanks again for the time today. High-level recap and proposed next steps below so we can align with your evaluation vs the hyperscalers: 

Recap from today's call:
- Primary eval focus: reliability & SLO behavior under production traffic (uptime, error budgets, rate limiting, burst handling, and failover across regions).
- Baseline comparisons: Acme will compare Redwood against their current hyperscaler endpoints (AWS/Azure) and one other inference API.
- Success criteria: observable failover without request loss, clear error-budget accounting, and predictable rate-limit behavior under burst + sustained load.

Proposed next tests (we can run these in your sandbox):
1) Sustained throughput: 30-minute run at 75% of expected peak QPS to check latency tail and KV cache behavior.
2) Burst/rate-limit test: controlled spike to 5x baseline for 2 minutes to validate throttling policy and 429/Retry-After semantics.
3) Failover: simulate regional outage (route to alternate region) and measure RPO/RTO for in-flight sessions.
4) Error-budget measurement: induce transient errors (rate limit + CPU backpressure) to ensure our error accounting and SLA math align with yours.

Attachments: redwood-slo-comparison.pdf (one-pager comparing our SLOs vs common hyperscalers), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (editable M.A.P.)

Next steps / asks: 
- Can you confirm a test window (preferred: Thu 03/05 between 09:00-12:00 PT)?
- Please share sandbox API key / endpoint and any constraints on load testing (IP allowlists, max test IPs).
- Which hyperscaler behavior is most important to replicate/beat (e.g., strict 429s vs soft throttling)?

I'll loop Rishi for the orchestration and Ben on commercial questions. Looking forward — we think these tests will demonstrate predictable failover and clear error-budget semantics compared to the hyperscalers.


Marissa Cole
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
[Attachment: redwood-slo-comparison.pdf (PDF, 1 page)]
[Attachment: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (Excel, 3 sheets)]

From: Jenna Smith <jenna.smith@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Acme Platform Team <platform@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reliability SLO follow-up / competitive evaluation

Thanks Marissa, appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before we lock a window: 

- Test window: Thu 03/05 09:00-12:00 PT works for us, but we need a 30-minute prep/handshake beforehand to exchange keys and IP ranges.
- KPIs we care most about: 99.95% sustained availability, 95th/99th latency tails under sustained load, and graceful degradation (no silent failures during region failover).
- Rate limits: we expect explicit 429s with Retry-After and a documented burst policy — opaque soft-throttles are a no-go for our platform.
- Compliance/logging: please provide audit log samples showing request IDs, response codes, and routing decisions for failover events.

Also attaching our internal test constraints doc (acme-test-constraints.docx). We'll need Redwood to sign the mutual action plan before the run — I'll ask procurement to start the DocuSign flow once we confirm timing.

On the comparisons vs hyperscalers: our incumbent exhibits eventual blackholing during region failover (requests dropped for ~30-90s). If you can show sub-10s failover for in-flight requests or clear retry guidance that recovers without customer-visible errors, that will be a strong differentiator.

I can join the prep call — do you want platform or engineering on the call as well?


Jenna Smith
CTO, Acme Corp
jenna.smith@acme.com | (617) 555-9988
[Attachment: acme-test-constraints.docx (DOCX, 2 pages)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Smith <jenna.smith@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reliability SLO follow-up / competitive evaluation

Thanks Jenna, quick internal note + suggestions (forwarding to keep everyone aligned).

Internal summary / proposed trade-offs: 
- Offer: We can commit to a 99.9% uptime SLA for the hosted endpoint in the sandbox evaluation period; for Dedicated customers we support 99.95%+ with reserved capacity. We should make the sandbox SLA explicit in the MAP.
- Rate-limits: we'll surface explicit 429s with Retry-After headers and provide a deterministic token-bucket config for the run (we can pre-share policy JSON). This is intentionally different from some hyperscaler soft-throttles.
- Failover: our smart routing will perform active region failover with sticky session forwarding when KV cache policies allow; worst-case RTO for in-flight tokens is typically <15s in our tests, but we should validate in Acme's environment.

Action items I suggest we own: 
- Rishi to prepare the SLO/test playbook and load harness (k6 script + simple replay harness).
- Marissa to coordinate procurement/MAP signature and confirm test window.
- Ben to draft a short SLA summary page for the sandbox run to attach to DocuSign.

I'll add the HubSpot deal and attach the SLA blurb.


Ben Carter
VP, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
[Internal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4782]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Smith <jenna.smith@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reliability SLO follow-up / competitive evaluation

Jenna / team, happy to run the tests. Quick plan and asks below.

Planned test checklist (details in attached slo-test-plan.md):
- Prep/Handshake (30m): exchange sandbox API key, allowed IPs, and test account.
- Sustained load (30m): run at ~75% peak QPS, capture 50/95/99 latencies and CPU/GPU metrics.
- Burst test (2m): spike to 5x for 2 minutes, confirm 429 semantics and Retry-After header behavior.
- Failover test: trigger region failover and measure RTO for in-flight requests; capture request IDs and routing decisions.
- Error-budget calculation: measure errors vs total requests and map to a daily error budget metric for your SLA.

Requests from our side:
- Please provide sandbox endpoint + API key (or a test bearer token) and an allowlist for our test IPs.
- If you have a representative payload set (typical prompt sizes / seq lengths), please share so our load harness matches your production patterns.

I'll attach the test plan and a small load script. We'll also record all logs and provide a sample audit log with request IDs post-run for your compliance team.

Proposed prep call: Thu 03/05 08:30 PT (30m), then tests at 09:00 PT. Confirm and I'll send the calendar invite + meeting notes.

Thanks
Rishi Malhotra
Staff Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
[Attachment: slo-test-plan.md (Markdown, 5 sections)]
[Attachment: load-harness-k6.tar.gz (TAR.GZ, test scripts)]
